text:
Using plain water for bladder washout can cause osmotic lysis of red blood cells and urothelial irritation, and in severe cases fluid absorption may lead to hemolysis, hyponatremia, and hypervolemia; sterile normal saline (or prescribed irrigation fluid) should be used instead. The main risk is hemolysis and electrolyte disturbance from hypotonic fluid absorption, especially with prolonged or high-volume irrigation or mucosal injury.
